script.title: XML vs JSON: A Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Hello, welcome to our quick look at XML and JSON. Imagine you have a small data structure like this: <root><name>John</name><age>30</age></root>. This is a simple XML structure. Let's see how it looks in JSON format: {"name": "John", "age": 30}. See how the structure is different? XML uses tags, like <name> and <age>, to define the structure. JSON uses curly braces and colons, like {name: "John", age: 30}. XML is like a tree with branches, while JSON is more like a list of key-value pairs. XML is great for complex data structures, like HTML or XML documents. JSON is better for simpler data, like API responses or configuration files. Which one you use depends on what you're working with and what you're trying to do with it. That's it for today's quick look at XML and JSON. Thanks for watching! 🌟 XML: <root><name>John</name><age>30</age></root> JSON: {"name": "John", "age": 30}. Both represent the same data, but in different ways.
